passageText: In Poetry Corner, students replaced plain words with vivid ones. They changed "walked" to "tiptoed" and "said" to "whispered." These choices helped readers imagine the scene more clearly. Strong word choice can make writing more lively and expressive.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best summarizes the passage?
questions.correctChoice: Vivid word choices make writing clearer and more expressive.
choices: Poems should use only simple words.
Vivid word choices make writing clearer and more expressive.
Students should avoid revising poems.
Tone never changes with word choice.

questions.prompt: In 2-3 sentences, explain one example of stronger word choice and its effect.

title: The Team Bench
missionLabel: Infer how classmates solved a friendship problem.
passageText: At recess, Lila noticed Jonah standing alone near the fence. She invited him to sit on the team bench and asked if he wanted to join a game. Jonah nodded but looked unsure. questions.prompt: What can readers infer about Lila?
questions.correctChoice: She noticed someone left out and helped him feel included.
choices: She wanted to play alone.
She noticed someone left out and helped him feel included.
She did not know game rules.
She ignored Jonah on purpose.

questions.prompt: Write two complete sentences explaining which details show kindness.

title: Classroom Agreement
missionLabel: Find main idea in a text about respectful communication.
passageText: The class created an agreement for group work. Students listen without interrupting, use respectful words, and ask questions kindly. If disagreements happen, they pause and restate each idea before choosing a solution. These habits help classmates feel heard and valued.

choices: Groups should avoid asking questions.
Respectful communication habits help groups work better together.

questions.prompt: In two sentences, explain why one agreement rule can prevent conflict.

missionLabel: Sequence events in a friendship story.

missionLabel: Infer how a written apology repaired a friendship.
passageText: Rosa accidentally erased Ben's drawing while cleaning the table. She felt upset and wrote a note that said she was sorry and wanted to help redraw the picture. Ben read the note and accepted her apology. They spent recess rebuilding the drawing together.

missionLabel: Use vocabulary in context about welcoming others.

missionLabel: Summarize data collection in a neighborhood project.

passageText: Naturalists look for tracks, scat, and nests to learn which animals live nearby. Tracks are footprints left in mud or snow. Scat is animal waste that can show what an animal eats. Reading these signs helps scientists study wildlife without disturbing it.
